title: cmdpal windows can be capture when invisible
author: huoyan1231

judgment.rationale: A Command Palette maintainer explained that the window is intentionally cloaked rather than destroyed so it can be summoned instantly, and that the screenshot application does not honor cloaking. The follow-up asks for an optional fully-hidden mode, which is an enhancement request rather than evidence of a PowerToys capture bug.
evidence: The report is specific to third-party screenshot software detecting the centered cloaked window.
The maintainer states that Command Palette uses window cloaking by design for instant summoning.
Two users ask for a switch that fully hides the window; no malfunction in normal Command Palette use is described.
judgment.recommended_action: Close the bug classification as by design and, if desired, track the fully-hidden switch as a separate enhancement.

fix_assessment.rationale: The observed capture behavior follows the documented cloaking design and the requested switch changes product behavior rather than fixing a demonstrated defect.

issue_context.summary: Some screenshot tools expose Command Palette's intentionally cloaked window; users are requesting a separate full-hide option.
known_information: Command Palette remains cloaked for fast activation.
The screenshot application does not account for cloaked windows.
Normal on-screen visibility is not reported.
inferences: A full-hide option could affect launch latency and should be evaluated as a feature request.
issue_context.analysis: The maintainer explanation resolves the bug claim. The remaining request should not stay framed as an Issue-Bug.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

actions.label: Clarify by-design cloaking
actions.note: Draft candidate only; no comment or other write was made to microsoft/PowerToys.

comment.body: Command Palette is intentionally cloaked rather than fully destroyed while dismissed so it can be summoned immediately. The reported screenshot application does not honor Windows cloaking, so this is not evidence that the palette is visibly open during normal use. A switch to fully hide or destroy the window would be a separate enhancement with possible startup-latency tradeoffs.
